triage.pre_fix_wrong_because: The §122 surcharge exception was gated on the witness exemplar flags `entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b`, identifiers that in the generated chapters also carry China-301 list-1 and §232-aluminum membership, so every §301-listed line was zeroed for all origins even though the rule's own proof atoms cite only the 9903.03.03 (aa)(ii) exclusion list and "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles provided for in headings 9903.82.02 and 9903.82.04" as exceptions.
triage.triage_notes: Reference module for this chunk; all 12 indices got the byte-identical substantive pattern. Six distinct formula edits per module: (1) section_122_component_rate gate entry_is_line_a/b -> entry_is_section_122_exempt/entry_is_section_232_covered (the defect the PR names); (2) section_201_component_rate entry_is_line_e -> entry_is_section_201_cspv, identifier-only since both branches return 0 (no runtime change); (3) section_232_aluminum_component_rate entry_is_line_b -> entry_is_section_232_aluminum in both versions; (4) china_section_301_component_rate exemplar flags -> per-list membership (list123 / 2024_action / list4a / solar), with entry_is_line_d retained for the beer/§338 term; (5) brazil_section_301_component_rate and (6) forced_labor_section_301_component_rate flipped from 'zero for exemplars a/b, else apply by origin' to an affirmative 'entry_is_*_301_listed and origin' gate. Note a doubt on (5)/(6): the module summary states those membership inputs default to declared-boolean FALSE because entry preparation cannot populate the lists, so the post-fix rules are always 0 in practice, whereas the cited source (9903.05.01, 'articles the product of Brazil', with enumerated exclusions) applies the duty unless excluded — arguably under-application, mitigated by both actions being post-window (2026-07-22/07-24). The module also gains ch73_s232_steel_heading_rate (0.50) and section_232_steel_component_rate added to schedule_statutory_stack — a separate unrepresented_clause-style fidelity gain. Two provenance caveats visible at this commit (both fixed later on the PR branch per the maintainer's issue comment): section_232_steel_component_rate's atoms are double-nested under metadata.proof.proof.atoms rather than metadata.proof.atoms, and the atoms cite us/statute/hts/9903.81.87/.88 while the PR body grounds the rate on the consolidated 9903.82.02 provision. Provision not read: resolve_provision.py returned {"error": "unresolved"} for us/statute/hts/9903.81.87 ('Corpus descendants for us/statute/hts cross active release scopes' / 'No active corpus source found'), so the 50% steel rate is unverified against the corpus; the §122 kind rests on the PR body plus the rule's unchanged proof atoms. a9562cfd44 is an intra-branch commit of PR #1300, not the squash merge. Alternative kind considered: wrong_entity_or_scope (the §122 exception applied to the wrong population of lines); I chose untraceable_branch because the pre-fix condition was an exemplar identifier with no basis in the cited §122 sources and the fix re-grounds it.
triage.verifier_justification: I tried to refute this as a pure identifier rename or an architecture-only "input surface generalization" and could not: within this one file at the parent commit, `entry_is_line_a` simultaneously zeroes the §122 surcharge (line 2572) and carries China-301 list-1 membership (line 2994), and `entry_is_line_b` simultaneously zeroes §122, gates §232 aluminum (2744/2751) and gates the China-301 2024 action (2995), so no caller population of those booleans can make all the rules correct at chapter scale — the fix splits one flag into several distinct identifiers rather than renaming it. The §122 rule's own exception atoms cite only the 9903.03.03 subdivision (aa)(ii) exclusion list, 7202.11.10, and the "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper or derivative aluminum or steel articles" carve-out; nothing in the cited source exempts §301-listed lines from the surcharge, so the pre-fix condition was a branch with no source basis and the fix re-grounds it to the two cited exception predicates. That is untraceable_branch rather than wrong_entity_or_scope or polarity_or_logic: the ungrounded thing is the condition itself, and the repair is re-grounding it on the provision the rule already cites. Mechanical is ruled out because formula tokens and runtime values change (the PR concedes a "principled exception class" of 18 witness-slice cells that differ precisely where "the witness's own coupling was the unlawful part").

triage.verifier_notes:
Corroboration is structural, not just narrative: at parent 29dbbdac05, `git show 29dbbdac05:us/policies/cbp/us-tariff-schedule/generated/ch73/ch73.yaml` line 2572 zeroes §122 on `entry_is_line_a or entry_is_line_b` while line 2994 uses `entry_is_line_a` as China-301 list-1 membership and 2995 uses `entry_is_line_b` as the 2024-action membership. The "unlawfully suppressed" wording is self-reported PR text from the same authoring agent (Claude Fable 5), so I leaned on the diff rather than the claim.

Caveats a reviewer should weigh:
1. The fix is partial. Post-fix the exemplar flags survive at lines 1908 (`entry_is_reciprocal_annex_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_a`), 1925 (`entry_is_reciprocal_metals_excluded: formula: entry_is_line_b`), 2368/2524 (`if origin_is_brazil and not entry_is_line_b` in the IEEPA reciprocal stack) and 2998 (`entry_is_line_d and origin_is_china` in the 301 sum). This does not make the repaired branch a non-defect, but the module is not fully decoupled.
2. The same diff bundles a second, separable change: new `ch73_s232_steel_heading_rate` (0.50) + `section_232_steel_component_rate`, wired into `schedule_statutory_stack`. That is added coverage (unrepresented_clause at best, or an enhancement outside the module's declared "same panel-projection component sequence as the witness total" scope), and per the PR it is the larger numeric effect (3.89pp). If the corpus wants one defect per module, the §122 re-grounding is the anchored and better-evidenced one; if it allows multiple, the steel component should be scored separately.
3. The Brazil and forced-labor rewrites are a different flavor again — they drop an ungrounded a/b exclusion *and* add a missing membership gate (`entry_is_brazil_301_listed`, `entry_is_forced_labor_301_listed`), with those inputs defaulting FALSE per the summary. Arguably unrepresented_clause for the added list gate.
4. The §201 CSPV hunk (`if entry_is_line_e: 0 else: 0` -> `if entry_is_section_201_cspv: 0 else: 0`) is runtime-inert — both branches return 0 — so it carries no fidelity weight.
5. Provenance check: through the pinned release `us-rulespec-2026-08-08-obbb-alien-snap` (corpus commit e79781bd), `us/statute/hts/chapter-99/page-221` resolves to note subdivisions (x)-(z) and page-230 to §232 steel TRQ notes — neither contains the (aa)(ii) 9903.03.03 excerpt or the "articles of aluminum, of steel, or of copper" excerpt the §122 atoms quote. Those atoms are unchanged by this diff (page indexing appears to have shifted between HTS revisions), so it does not affect the verdict, but a reviewer relying on atom excerpt/page alignment should not treat those paths as verified.
